subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What do the arrows in a food chain represent?
options: The total biomass at each level
questions.explain: Arrows point from the organism being eaten to the one eating it, showing the transfer of energy along the chain.

questions.q: Which term describes an organism that makes its own food by photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Producers, such as green plants, make their own food by photosynthesis and form the base of a food chain.

questions.q: In a food chain, the first trophic level is always occupied by which type of organism?
questions.explain: Producers occupy the first trophic level because they trap light energy and make food for the rest of the chain.

questions.q: What is the original source of energy for almost all food chains?
questions.explain: Light energy from the Sun is captured by producers during photosynthesis and passed along the chain.

questions.q: Which process releases energy as heat and reduces the energy passed on to the next trophic level?
questions.explain: Respiration releases energy as heat to the surroundings, so this energy is not available to the next trophic level.

questions.q: Which bacteria convert nitrogen gas from the air into nitrogen compounds in the soil?
questions.explain: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert unreactive nitrogen gas into nitrogen compounds that plants can use.

questions.q: Which process returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere when fossil fuels are burned?
questions.explain: Combustion of fossil fuels releases stored carbon back into the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to collect small invertebrates such as insects?
questions.explain: A pooter uses suction through a tube to collect small invertebrates without harming them.

questions.q: Why is a food web a more realistic model than a single food chain?
options: It shows that organisms feed on, and are eaten by, several different species
It shows the exact number of each organism
It includes only the producers in a habitat
It shows how energy is created by consumers
questions.explain: A food web links many food chains together, showing the interconnected feeding relationships in a habitat.

questions.q: Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels?
options: So much energy is lost at each level that too little remains to support further levels
Predators cannot find enough prey to hunt
There are not enough producers on Earth
questions.explain: Because most energy is lost at each transfer, there is eventually not enough left to support another trophic level.

questions.q: Which of the following is a way that energy is lost between trophic levels?
options: Energy released as heat during respiration
Energy gained directly from the Sun
questions.explain: Energy is lost between levels through respiration, movement, heat and egestion, so less passes on.

questions.q: What is the role of decomposers in the carbon cycle?
options: They release carbon dioxide back into the air as they respire while breaking down dead organisms
They fix nitrogen gas from the air
They photosynthesise to remove carbon dioxide
They convert nitrates into nitrogen gas
questions.explain: As decomposers break down dead material they respire, returning carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.

questions.q: What do denitrifying bacteria do in the nitrogen cycle?
options: Convert nitrates in the soil back into nitrogen gas
Break down dead animals and plants
questions.explain: Denitrifying bacteria convert soil nitrates into nitrogen gas, returning nitrogen to the atmosphere.

questions.q: Why should quadrats be placed randomly when sampling an area?
options: To avoid bias so the sample is representative of the whole area
To make the organisms easier to count
To ensure the same species is always found
To increase the number of organisms collected
questions.explain: Random placement prevents bias, so results give a fair estimate for the whole habitat.

questions.q: What does a pyramid of biomass represent?
options: The mass of living material at each trophic level
The number of organisms at each trophic level
The energy created at each trophic level
The number of different species in a habitat
questions.explain: A pyramid of biomass shows the total dry mass of living material at each trophic level.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of energy is typically transferred from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explain: Roughly 90% of energy is lost through respiration, movement, heat and egestion, so only about 10% passes on.

questions.q: In a capture-recapture study, 40 woodlice were caught, marked and released. Later, 50 woodlice were caught, of which 10 were marked. What is the estimated total population?
questions.explain: Population = (first sample x second sample) / number marked in second = (40 x 50) / 10 = 200.

questions.q: A student counts a mean of 8 dandelions per 1 m2 quadrat. Estimate the number of dandelions in a 200 m2 field.
questions.explain: Multiply the mean per square metre by the total area: 8 x 200 = 1600.

questions.q: In the food chain grass to grasshopper to frog to snake, which organism is the secondary consumer?
questions.explain: The secondary consumer eats the primary consumer, so the frog (which eats the grasshopper) is the secondary consumer.

questions.q: A plant traps 20 000 kJ of energy. A caterpillar that eats the plant stores 2 000 kJ. What is the efficiency of energy transfer?
questions.explain: Efficiency = (energy transferred / energy taken in) x 100 = (2000 / 20000) x 100 = 10%.
